page: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute workloads, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1926.0 and a multi-core score of 7695.0. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. Single-threaded gzip compression performs strongly at 32.73 GB/sec, and text processing also ranks in the top 25% with a Geekbench score of 2743.0. However, memory performance is a relative bottleneck, with the Passmark memory score falling into the bottom 25% at 1800.86, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measuring 47.98 GB/sec.

Given its compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, the c7i.2xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, text processing, and lightweight machine learning inference using small to medium models. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM text generation due to its lower memory density and weaker uncached memory performance.
